[27:52] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): Last one. Can we trigger a workflow manually for a one-off exception?

[28:05] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me summarise what I heard, and correct me. You don't need automation for its own sake. The opportunity is making a small number of cross-system processes observable, easier to change, and less dependent on specific individuals. The pilot has to prove integration reliability, exception handling, governance, and that there's a credible operating model on your side.
[28:31] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): Yes. And keep the first workflow narrow. I'd rather have one thing we trust than six demos.
[28:39] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): Can you also write down the assumptions you made today? Some of what we told you was approximate and I don't want it hardening into requirements by accident.
[28:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Will do. Written recap with open questions separated from confirmed requirements.
[28:58] Rachel Morgan (VP Revenue Operations, Acme Logistics): Great. Send it over and we'll come back with sample inputs. Thanks both.
[29:04] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Thanks.
[29:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thanks. And Tom — good luck with the dog.
[29:10] Tom Alvarez (Director of Customer Success, Acme Logistics): [laughs] Cheers.

context.text:
=== CALL-014 (call kind: churn)
CALL ID: CALL-014
DATE: 2026-09-18
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
CUSTOMER: Verity Payments
INDUSTRY: Payments
COMPANY SIZE: 800 employees
STAGE: Churn post-mortem
DURATION: 21 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Ruth Adeyemi, Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow
- Kwame Boateng, Head of Operations, Verity Payments
- Sarah Lindqvist, Engineering Manager, Verity Payments
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Kwame, Sarah — thank you for doing this. You didn't have to.
[00:05] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We nearly didn't, if I'm honest.
[00:08] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I know. And I want to set expectations: this isn't a save attempt. You've signed with Workato, the decision's made, and I'm not going to spend twenty minutes trying to reopen it.
[00:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Good. That was my concern.
[00:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What I want is to understand what went wrong properly, because two years is a long time to get something wrong and I'd like to not do it again.
[00:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We'll be honest then.
[00:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please be.
[00:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd add — I took over this account in January, so about eight months ago. Some of what went wrong predates me and some of it doesn't, and I'd rather you told me which is which.
[00:55] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Alright. Where do you want to start?
[00:59] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): With the decision. When did you actually decide?
[01:04] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Properly? June.
[01:07] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): June.
[01:09] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Though I'd say the decision became inevitable in about February and it took us until June to admit it.
[01:17] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): February.
[01:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): February.
[01:21] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a month after I took the account.
[01:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not about you. I want to be clear about that.
[01:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd still like to know what happened in February.
[01:33] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): February was when we tried to build the settlement reconciliation workflow and couldn't.
[01:40] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Couldn't, or found it hard?
[01:43] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Couldn't, in the sense that the effort exceeded the value by a factor I couldn't justify to my team.
[01:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Tell me about it specifically.
[01:54] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Our settlement provider is a mid-sized European processor. You don't have a connector for them. Nobody does, to be fair — Workato doesn't either.
[02:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So what was the difference?
[02:09] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The difference is that we ended up writing a custom integration either way, and once you've accepted you're writing custom integrations, you start asking what the platform is actually giving you.
[02:24] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And what was the answer?
[02:26] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Orchestration and run history, which are genuinely good. But not enough on their own for what we were paying.
[02:35] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): And this is where I'd push back on Sarah slightly.
[02:39] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Go on.
[02:41] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The connector gap was real. But it wasn't why we left. It was the thing we pointed at.
[02:49] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was the real reason?
[02:52] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Nobody in operations ever built anything.
[02:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Say more.
[02:59] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The entire pitch — and this is the pitch I bought, so I'm implicating myself — was that my team would own their own workflows. That we'd stop queuing behind engineering. Two years in, every single production workflow was built by Sarah's team.
[03:19] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Every one.
[03:21] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [crosstalk] So we paid a premium for a business-user platform and used it as an engineering tool. And as an engineering tool it's fine but it's not worth the premium.
[03:34] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Why didn't your team build?
[03:37] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] A few reasons and none of them are flattering.
[03:42] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather have unflattering.
[03:45] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The first workflow anyone builds is hard. Not conceptually hard — fiddly. You have to understand connections, you have to understand how data moves between steps, you have to understand what happens when something's null. My operations people are good at operations. They're not good at that, and expecting them to become good at it in their spare time was naive.
[04:11] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Did you have enablement?
[04:13] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We had a two-day onboarding at the start. Eight people attended. Six of them never touched it again.
[04:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And after that?
[04:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Nothing, until you arrived in January and offered some sessions.
[04:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Which you declined.
[04:31] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which I declined, because by January I'd already half-concluded it wasn't going to work and I didn't want to spend my team's time on it.
[04:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's useful and it's painful.
[04:46] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You asked.
[04:48] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I did ask. What would have changed it? If I'd arrived in month three rather than month twenty?
[04:56] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Honestly, I think if someone had sat with two of my people for a week in the first quarter and got them to ship something real, we'd still be a customer.
[05:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I agree with that.
[05:10] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Not a training course. Sitting with them. Building the actual thing they needed.
[05:17] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We do offer that.
[05:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Do you? Nobody ever offered it to me.
[05:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] It's a paid professional services engagement.
[05:28] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Ah.
[05:30] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which is possibly the problem. If the thing that makes the product succeed is a paid add-on, and the customer doesn't know they need it until it's too late —
[05:41] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Then you've designed a product that fails by default for people like me.
[05:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a harsher way of putting it than I would have, but I can't argue with it.
[05:53] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I add the engineering perspective? Because it's different.
[05:58] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please.
[06:00] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): My team quite liked it. The run history is genuinely better than what we'd have built. The exception queues are good. When something failed at three in the morning, we could see why, and that's not nothing.
[06:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So why did you support leaving?
[06:19] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Because we were maintaining custom integrations to a platform whose main selling point was that we wouldn't have to maintain custom integrations. And because the licence cost was being justified by a benefit — business-user autonomy — that wasn't materialising.
[06:39] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Say the other thing.
[06:41] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] And because two of my engineers wanted to build it in-house and I spent eighteen months arguing against them, and eventually I ran out of arguments.
[06:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was your last argument?
[06:56] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Maintenance. It's always maintenance. And it's a good argument right up until the platform also requires maintenance, at which point you're comparing two maintenance burdens and one of them costs a hundred thousand a year.
[07:13] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is that what you're paying Workato?
[07:16] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Less. Not dramatically less.
[07:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So it isn't a price decision.
[07:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's partly a price decision, because at the margin we could justify one and not the other. But no, it's not primarily price.
[07:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then what tipped it to Workato specifically?
[07:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Two things. Their connector for our core banking platform is genuinely better than yours. That one's just true.
[07:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It is true. We know.
[07:49] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): And their engineering-facing story is stronger. Recipes as code, better CI story, our engineers had opinions about it and the opinions were positive.
[08:02] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So you've bought an engineering tool.
[08:05] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] Yes. That's fair. We've bought an engineering tool and stopped pretending.
[08:12] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which is the honest conclusion. My team is never going to build workflows. That was my ambition and it was wrong, and rather than keep paying for the ambition I've accepted the reality.
[08:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask — do you think that ambition was wrong in principle, or wrong for Verity?
[08:33] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] For Verity. I've seen it work elsewhere. I was at a retailer before this where the operations team genuinely did build their own things.
[08:45] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was different?
[08:47] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): There was a person whose job it was. Not a champion, not an enthusiast — a role, with a title, whose entire job was building and maintaining automations for the business. Half a headcount, maybe.
[09:04] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We never had that.
[09:06] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We never had that and I never asked for it, because I thought the product removed the need for it.
[09:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's — I want to write that down properly, because I think it's the most important thing you've said.
[09:21] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which part?
[09:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That the product doesn't remove the need for the role. It changes what the role has to be good at.
[09:31] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Yes. That's exactly it.
[09:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): We do say that, in fairness. It's in the operating model guidance.
[09:40] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Is it? I've never seen the operating model guidance.
[09:44] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Then we don't say it, do we.
[09:48] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [laughs] Not effectively.
[09:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me ask about the sales process, since I ran it. What did I get wrong?
[09:58] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You want honesty on this too?
[10:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Especially on this.
[10:03] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You sold to my enthusiasm rather than to my capability. I was excited, I said my team would own it, and nobody in your organisation asked "who specifically, and what else is on their plate?"
[10:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a fair criticism.
[10:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not that you lied. You just believed me, and you shouldn't have, because I didn't know what I was agreeing to.
[10:31] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've started asking that question, for what it's worth. Not because of you — I don't want to claim that. But it's in my discovery now. "Name the person who'll build the second workflow."
[10:45] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): That's a good question. I wouldn't have had an answer.
[10:50] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the point of it.
[10:52] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I raise the support thing? Since we're doing grievances.
[10:57] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Go ahead.
[11:00] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The support was inconsistent. Some tickets came back in an hour with someone who clearly understood the product. Others came back in a day with a link to documentation I'd already read and cited in the ticket.
[11:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a known problem and it's a triage problem rather than a capability problem.
[11:23] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I assumed as much. It's not why we left. But it contributed to a general feeling that we were a small account.
[11:33] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Were you treated as a small account?
[11:36] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] Probably accurately, yes.
[11:40] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's the answer, isn't it. You were an eighty-thousand-pound account in a book of accounts where that's below median.
[11:50] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): I'd worked that out.
[11:52] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Most customers do.
[11:55] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is there anything we could have done in the last six months? Genuinely, not rhetorically.
[12:02] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Probably not. By March we'd started the Workato evaluation and once that starts it has its own momentum. People invest in it, they want to be right.
[12:16] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): There was a moment in April.
[12:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Was there?
[12:21] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): When the Workato PoC hit the same connector problem we'd hit with you. For about two weeks it looked like we'd have the same issue either way.
[12:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What happened?
[12:35] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): They put a solutions architect on it for three days and built us a working custom connector as part of the evaluation. Not billed.
[12:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Ah.
[12:49] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That's when it was over, if you want the specific moment.
[12:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Did anyone from our side know about the connector problem in April?
[12:59] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I mentioned it on a call. Not as an emergency. As a thing I was dealing with.
[13:06] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I remember that call.
[13:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): You said you'd look into whether there was a template.
[13:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And I did, and there wasn't, and I emailed you saying there wasn't.
[13:18] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): You did. That was an accurate and completely useless answer.
[13:23] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Yes. It was.
[13:26] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I'm not attacking you. You answered the question I asked. It's just that the right response wasn't answering the question.
[13:36] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The right response was three days of an SE.
[13:40] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The right response was three days of an SE, yes.
[13:44] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Would we have done that?
[13:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): For an eighty-thousand-pound account at renewal risk? [pause] I'd have had to argue for it. I might have lost.
[13:56] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a thing I'm going to raise internally.
[13:59] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): For what it's worth, I don't think you should have kept us. I think we were the wrong customer for the product, or the product was sold to us for the wrong reason.
[14:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which of those?
[14:13] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Both, slightly.
[14:16] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Alright. Let me ask about the practical side. What do you need from us for the exit?
[14:23] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Workflow definitions and run history exported. I've already pulled the definitions through the API and they came out fine.
[14:32] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Run history?
[14:34] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That's the one I want to check. We need eighteen months of run records for audit purposes. Not for Workato — for our own compliance.
[14:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Through the run events API. I'll send the pagination details because eighteen months is a lot of records and people usually hit a limit and assume it's broken.
[14:57] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That would be useful.
[15:00] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): How long do you need access after the contract ends?
[15:04] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): When does it end?
[15:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thirty-first of October.
[15:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I'd want until the end of November to be safe. The export will take longer than anyone thinks.
[15:15] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I can do read-only access through November at no charge. I'd rather you had a clean exit than a scramble.
[15:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You'd do that?
[15:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Yes, and I'd do it for two reasons. One, it's the right thing. Two, you'll be at another company in three years.
[15:36] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [laughs] That's very honest.
[15:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's both true things at once.
[15:42] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): I appreciate it either way.
[15:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And data deletion afterwards? You'll want that documented.
[15:50] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Yes. Our compliance team will ask for a deletion certificate.
[15:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll get that arranged and I'll tell you the timeline for it rather than saying "shortly after termination."
[16:04] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Thank you.
[16:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Anything else practical?
[16:09] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): There are two workflows still running that we haven't migrated. They'll be done by mid-October.
[16:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What are they?
[16:18] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Merchant onboarding notifications and a daily reconciliation report.
[16:24] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Neither of which will break anything if they stop.
[16:28] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The reconciliation one would be noticed. Not catastrophically.

[04:05] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Can I correct something Sophie said in the email, actually?

[07:43] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): It's more than four.
[07:45] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): [crosstalk] I know it's more than four. I'm being generous to my own argument.

[09:25] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll take it.
[09:27] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): What about visibility of who owns what? Because the dead-employee problem is real.

[09:49] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): We don't have a dev workspace. We don't have a dev anything.
[09:54] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] You'd get one. That's not extra cost, it's just how it's structured.

[15:13] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'm not saying no.

[15:56] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): If I don't, you'll find out in month two and then I've lost you anyway.
[16:02] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Alright. Marcus, can you do the logging thing?
[16:06] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): I can do the logging thing.

[28:36] Darren Wu (Director of Business Intelligence, Inkwell Learning): Add it to the written list.

[29:40] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Largely, yes. What I'd say is that this platform makes it possible. It doesn't make it happen.

[29:57] Darren Wu (Director of Business Intelligence, Inkwell Learning): People have.
[29:59] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): I'm sure.
[30:02] Darren Wu (Director of Business Intelligence, Inkwell Learning): Alright. I'll do the backward analysis and I'll be honest about what it shows. If the signal's not there I'll say so and we'll stop.
[30:13] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's all I'd want.
[30:16] Darren Wu (Director of Business Intelligence, Inkwell Learning): And if it is there, I'll be more enthusiastic than I've been today.
[30:22] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): You've been fine. Sceptical isn't unfriendly.

=== CALL-014 (call kind: churn)
CALL ID: CALL-014
DATE: 2026-09-18
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
CUSTOMER: Verity Payments
INDUSTRY: Payments
COMPANY SIZE: 800 employees
STAGE: Churn post-mortem
DURATION: 21 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Ruth Adeyemi, Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow
- Kwame Boateng, Head of Operations, Verity Payments
- Sarah Lindqvist, Engineering Manager, Verity Payments
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Kwame, Sarah — thank you for doing this. You didn't have to.
[00:05] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We nearly didn't, if I'm honest.
[00:08] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I know. And I want to set expectations: this isn't a save attempt. You've signed with Workato, the decision's made, and I'm not going to spend twenty minutes trying to reopen it.
[00:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Good. That was my concern.
[00:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What I want is to understand what went wrong properly, because two years is a long time to get something wrong and I'd like to not do it again.
[00:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We'll be honest then.
[00:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please be.
[00:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd add — I took over this account in January, so about eight months ago. Some of what went wrong predates me and some of it doesn't, and I'd rather you told me which is which.
[00:55] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Alright. Where do you want to start?
[00:59] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): With the decision. When did you actually decide?
[01:04] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Properly? June.
[01:07] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): June.
[01:09] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Though I'd say the decision became inevitable in about February and it took us until June to admit it.
[01:17] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): February.
[01:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): February.
[01:21] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a month after I took the account.
[01:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not about you. I want to be clear about that.
[01:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd still like to know what happened in February.
[01:33] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): February was when we tried to build the settlement reconciliation workflow and couldn't.
[01:40] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Couldn't, or found it hard?
[01:43] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Couldn't, in the sense that the effort exceeded the value by a factor I couldn't justify to my team.
[01:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Tell me about it specifically.
[01:54] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Our settlement provider is a mid-sized European processor. You don't have a connector for them. Nobody does, to be fair — Workato doesn't either.
[02:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So what was the difference?
[02:09] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The difference is that we ended up writing a custom integration either way, and once you've accepted you're writing custom integrations, you start asking what the platform is actually giving you.
[02:24] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And what was the answer?
[02:26] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Orchestration and run history, which are genuinely good. But not enough on their own for what we were paying.
[02:35] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): And this is where I'd push back on Sarah slightly.
[02:39] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Go on.
[02:41] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The connector gap was real. But it wasn't why we left. It was the thing we pointed at.
[02:49] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was the real reason?
[02:52] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Nobody in operations ever built anything.
[02:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Say more.
[02:59] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The entire pitch — and this is the pitch I bought, so I'm implicating myself — was that my team would own their own workflows. That we'd stop queuing behind engineering. Two years in, every single production workflow was built by Sarah's team.
[03:19] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Every one.
[03:21] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [crosstalk] So we paid a premium for a business-user platform and used it as an engineering tool. And as an engineering tool it's fine but it's not worth the premium.
[03:34] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Why didn't your team build?
[03:37] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] A few reasons and none of them are flattering.
[03:42] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather have unflattering.
[03:45] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The first workflow anyone builds is hard. Not conceptually hard — fiddly. You have to understand connections, you have to understand how data moves between steps, you have to understand what happens when something's null. My operations people are good at operations. They're not good at that, and expecting them to become good at it in their spare time was naive.
[04:11] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Did you have enablement?
[04:13] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We had a two-day onboarding at the start. Eight people attended. Six of them never touched it again.
[04:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And after that?
[04:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Nothing, until you arrived in January and offered some sessions.
[04:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Which you declined.
[04:31] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which I declined, because by January I'd already half-concluded it wasn't going to work and I didn't want to spend my team's time on it.
[04:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's useful and it's painful.
[04:46] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You asked.
[04:48] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I did ask. What would have changed it? If I'd arrived in month three rather than month twenty?
[04:56] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Honestly, I think if someone had sat with two of my people for a week in the first quarter and got them to ship something real, we'd still be a customer.
[05:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I agree with that.
[05:10] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Not a training course. Sitting with them. Building the actual thing they needed.
[05:17] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We do offer that.
[05:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Do you? Nobody ever offered it to me.
[05:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] It's a paid professional services engagement.
[05:28] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Ah.
[05:30] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which is possibly the problem. If the thing that makes the product succeed is a paid add-on, and the customer doesn't know they need it until it's too late —
[05:41] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Then you've designed a product that fails by default for people like me.
[05:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a harsher way of putting it than I would have, but I can't argue with it.
[05:53] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I add the engineering perspective? Because it's different.
[05:58] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please.
[06:00] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): My team quite liked it. The run history is genuinely better than what we'd have built. The exception queues are good. When something failed at three in the morning, we could see why, and that's not nothing.
[06:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So why did you support leaving?
[06:19] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Because we were maintaining custom integrations to a platform whose main selling point was that we wouldn't have to maintain custom integrations. And because the licence cost was being justified by a benefit — business-user autonomy — that wasn't materialising.
[06:39] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Say the other thing.
[06:41] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] And because two of my engineers wanted to build it in-house and I spent eighteen months arguing against them, and eventually I ran out of arguments.
[06:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was your last argument?
[06:56] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Maintenance. It's always maintenance. And it's a good argument right up until the platform also requires maintenance, at which point you're comparing two maintenance burdens and one of them costs a hundred thousand a year.
[07:13] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is that what you're paying Workato?
[07:16] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Less. Not dramatically less.
[07:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So it isn't a price decision.
[07:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's partly a price decision, because at the margin we could justify one and not the other. But no, it's not primarily price.
[07:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then what tipped it to Workato specifically?
[07:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Two things. Their connector for our core banking platform is genuinely better than yours. That one's just true.
[07:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It is true. We know.
[07:49] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): And their engineering-facing story is stronger. Recipes as code, better CI story, our engineers had opinions about it and the opinions were positive.
[08:02] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So you've bought an engineering tool.
[08:05] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] Yes. That's fair. We've bought an engineering tool and stopped pretending.
[08:12] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which is the honest conclusion. My team is never going to build workflows. That was my ambition and it was wrong, and rather than keep paying for the ambition I've accepted the reality.
[08:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask — do you think that ambition was wrong in principle, or wrong for Verity?
[08:33] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] For Verity. I've seen it work elsewhere. I was at a retailer before this where the operations team genuinely did build their own things.
[08:45] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was different?
[08:47] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): There was a person whose job it was. Not a champion, not an enthusiast — a role, with a title, whose entire job was building and maintaining automations for the business. Half a headcount, maybe.
[09:04] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We never had that.
[09:06] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We never had that and I never asked for it, because I thought the product removed the need for it.
[09:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's — I want to write that down properly, because I think it's the most important thing you've said.
[09:21] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which part?
[09:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That the product doesn't remove the need for the role. It changes what the role has to be good at.
[09:31] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Yes. That's exactly it.
[09:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): We do say that, in fairness. It's in the operating model guidance.
[09:40] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Is it? I've never seen the operating model guidance.
[09:44] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Then we don't say it, do we.
[09:48] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [laughs] Not effectively.
[09:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me ask about the sales process, since I ran it. What did I get wrong?
[09:58] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You want honesty on this too?
[10:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Especially on this.
[10:03] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You sold to my enthusiasm rather than to my capability. I was excited, I said my team would own it, and nobody in your organisation asked "who specifically, and what else is on their plate?"
[10:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a fair criticism.
[10:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not that you lied. You just believed me, and you shouldn't have, because I didn't know what I was agreeing to.
[10:31] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've started asking that question, for what it's worth. Not because of you — I don't want to claim that. But it's in my discovery now. "Name the person who'll build the second workflow."
[10:45] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): That's a good question. I wouldn't have had an answer.
[10:50] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the point of it.
[10:52] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I raise the support thing? Since we're doing grievances.
[10:57] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Go ahead.
[11:00] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The support was inconsistent. Some tickets came back in an hour with someone who clearly understood the product. Others came back in a day with a link to documentation I'd already read and cited in the ticket.
[11:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a known problem and it's a triage problem rather than a capability problem.
[11:23] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I assumed as much. It's not why we left. But it contributed to a general feeling that we were a small account.

[11:36] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] Probably accurately, yes.
[11:40] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's the answer, isn't it. You were an eighty-thousand-pound account in a book of accounts where that's below median.
[11:50] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): I'd worked that out.
[11:52] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Most customers do.
[11:55] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is there anything we could have done in the last six months? Genuinely, not rhetorically.
[12:02] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Probably not. By March we'd started the Workato evaluation and once that starts it has its own momentum. People invest in it, they want to be right.
[12:16] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): There was a moment in April.
[12:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Was there?
[12:21] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): When the Workato PoC hit the same connector problem we'd hit with you. For about two weeks it looked like we'd have the same issue either way.

[12:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Ah.
[12:49] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That's when it was over, if you want the specific moment.
[12:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Did anyone from our side know about the connector problem in April?
[12:59] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I mentioned it on a call. Not as an emergency. As a thing I was dealing with.
[13:06] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I remember that call.
[13:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): You said you'd look into whether there was a template.
[13:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And I did, and there wasn't, and I emailed you saying there wasn't.
[13:18] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): You did. That was an accurate and completely useless answer.
[13:23] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Yes. It was.
[13:26] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I'm not attacking you. You answered the question I asked. It's just that the right response wasn't answering the question.
[13:36] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The right response was three days of an SE.
